Articles

Get started

Get started

Take a layer of points to cells with standard errors, a score from spatial cross-validation and a map that marks where its predictions apply.

Step by step

One step of the pipeline per article, in the order you take them.

Choosing a resolution

Decide how many cells the data support, and pass that count to the tessellation.

Building cells and summarising them

Draw the cells, put each observation in one, and report each cell’s value with the right standard error.

Spatial cross-validation

Choose folds whose score matches the map you will make, size the blocks, and read every part of the result.

Fitting and checking models

Pick a backend or write your own, compare backends on the same folds, check the residuals, and map where the predictions apply.

Exporting and reporting results

Write the cells to a file others can join to, and report the numbers that say how far a cell value or a map can be trusted.

Worked example

Worked example: North Carolina

The pipeline on a simulated field over North Carolina, comparing four tessellations, two fold schemes and two backends at cell counts set by hand.

Help

Pages to consult when a step fails or a term is unclear.

Troubleshooting and performance

The errors and warnings you are most likely to meet, what each means, and how to handle large layers, parallel folds, caches and the log.

Terms used on these pages

Short definitions of the terms the articles and help pages use.
